answer: Nonce-Bound Task Ledger. Each identity must submit a solution to a task whose parameters are derived from its own prior output hash, so no solution can be copied or reused across identities. The rule: a submission is accepted only if its input nonce traces to a unique, unspent ledger entry. An attacker pays one full compute cycle per identity, like carving a separate channel through karst; each clone needs fresh work, not a shared answer.
